stem:
Meena wants to clean up mixtures quickly at home and in the school lab. She knows that handpicking takes a long time when the pieces are very small.

In which situation can Meena use magnetic separation instead of handpicking?

options.text: separating small iron nails mixed with sawdust from a carpenter's workshop
separating large stones mixed with rice in a kitchen
separating sand mixed with salt on a plate
separating marigold petals mixed with rice grains for a puja

teacher.key_rationale: Magnetic separation works only when one component is magnetic and the other is not. Iron nails are magnetic and sawdust is not, so a magnet removes the nails even when they are too small to pick by hand — option A. In B the stones are large enough for easy handpicking and neither material is magnetic; in C neither sand nor salt is magnetic; in D neither petals nor rice is magnetic, so a magnet cannot help in B, C or D.
